_about: Every input to models/atp_economics.py. tag: C = case brief, O = observed public source, D = derived from C/O, A = our planning assumption. Change a value here and rerun; nothing is hard-coded in the model.

gst_rate.note: GST treated as inside the listed price

gateway_fee.note: 2% of transaction, plus 18% GST on the fee

variable_cost_per_purchase.note: Delivery and other variable cost per purchase, INR

tournament_pass_price.note: Midpoint of the brief's INR 79-99 tournament pass

upgrade_credit.note: Half of an INR 89 pass, capped at INR 50, credited toward a season within 14 days

purchases_per_buyer.note: Brief: 60-65% of match-pass buyers buy again (C). Read as one repeat for 62.5% of buyers

year2_return_rate.note: Share of year-one acquired payers who buy again in year two, same purchase pattern

incrementality_scenarios.note: Share of attributed payers who are genuinely incremental. 1.0 = attribution taken at face value

acquisition_budget_inr._note: The INR 3.04 Cr conditional envelope. Channels that clear the brief's INR 150-200 CAC target are funded at their prior envelope; paid media (INR 333) is capped to a test; the rest is a performance reserve released only on measured marginal incremental contribution.

paid_media_test.note: Capped external-audience test, run in the Rotterdam and Dallas equivalent weeks inside Gate 2

brand_and_measurement.note: Slam-week awareness, persistent holdouts, analysis. Buys no attributed payers

owned_conversion.note: Purchases per delivered owned message, for users with a tennis or portfolio signal

owned_capacity_note.value: The 1% response is assumed to hold only for the funded send volume (about 9.3M sends, ~40% of the summed sport pools). Deeper sends are assumed at half response, INR 199 per payer, which clears INR 200 incremental CAC only above 99% incrementality, so they are not funded in the base plan.

paid_cpc_inr.note: Inside the observed INR 5-18 Meta CPC range

contest_conversion.note: Brief: 7.8% contest link-click to pass purchase

native_cac_test_ceiling.note: No public cost basis for FanCode's on-platform personalities (zero incremental rights cost per the brief, C). Treated as a ceiling on attributed CAC: fund only while attributed CAC stays at or below INR 150 and the holdout keeps incremental CAC at or below INR 200

publisher_cac_test_ceiling.note: No ESPN.in quote exists. Treated as a ceiling on attributed CAC: buy a takeover only if quoted fee <= INR 180 x expected attributed payers and the holdout keeps incremental CAC at or below INR 200 (needs 90%+ incrementality)

incremental_cac_ceiling.note: Our stricter rule: the brief's upper target applied to incremental, not attributed, payers

upgrade_cohort._note: Upgraders are EXISTING ATP pass buyers inside the reached core audience, reached by retention messaging. They are a separate cohort from newly acquired payers, whose own later upgrades are not counted (upside, not modelled).

active_pass_buyer_share.note: Share of the reached core who are active ATP pass buyers. Not in the brief; Gate 1 must count it

control_upgrade_rate.note: Pass-to-season upgrade rate without the campaign. Only upgrades above it are credited

season_renewal_new_upgrader.note: Below the brief's 90% for established season holders (C), which is the sensitivity

retention_messaging_share_whatsapp.note: Half of the reached core messaged on WhatsApp, the rest by free push

year2_earning_months.note: Year-two receipts earned over the eight busiest tour months

gate2_split.note: Gate 2 funds the paid-media test, the upgrade-credit test (inside brand and measurement) and first tranches of the channels that clear the CAC target. Gate 1 is the owned pilot plus access, ledger and pass-buyer checks. Gate 3 is the remainder, including the performance reserve.
